test_title: PYST 18: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements with respect to Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT) in India is/are correct?

 1. DDT was a tax on dividends paid to the shareholders of a company.

 2. Budget 2025-26 has proposed to remove the DDT paid by the companies to investors.

 3. DDT was removed to avoid double taxation of dividends and make the Indian Equity Market more attractive.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT)** was a tax levied on companies, requiring them to pay a tax on the dividends distributed to shareholders.
 
• The **Finance Act 2020**, not Budget 2025-26, abolished DDT, shifting the tax burden to shareholders who now pay tax on dividends according to their applicable income tax slab.
 
• The removal of DDT was aimed at **avoiding double taxation of dividends**, as earlier companies paid DDT and shareholders also paid taxes on dividends.
 
• This reform was introduced to make the Indian equity market more **investor-friendly** and attract foreign and domestic investments.
 
• DDT was earlier charged at an effective rate of **20.56%** (including surcharge and cess).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **What is Double Taxation?**

 
 
• Double taxation occurs when the same income is taxed twice. Under the old DDT regime, companies paid tax on their profits, and shareholders paid tax on the dividends received.
 
 
 
• **Current Taxation on Dividends:**
 
 
• Post-2020, dividends are taxed in the hands of shareholders based on their applicable income tax slab rates.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs):**
 
 
• The removal of DDT has benefitted FPIs as they can now avail of benefits under tax treaties, reducing their tax burden.
 
 
 
• **Finance Act 2020:**
 
 
• This act introduced key reforms, including the abolition of DDT, to simplify tax structures and boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Attractiveness of Equity Markets:**
 
 
• Removing DDT aligns India’s taxation policies with global practices, making Indian equity markets more competitive and attractive to investors.
